name: Spirit rover
tagline: Spirit’s wheels finally sank into Martian soil, but the rover’s discoveries had already carried the mission far beyond its design.
imageAlt: Illustrated archive portrait of Spirit rover
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Explore Gusev Crater and look for signs that liquid water once shaped the surface.
beats.achieved: It was built for about 90 Martian days but worked for years, studying rocks and soil that showed Mars had a wetter past.
beats.ending: In 2009 it broke through soft sand and became stuck. Engineers tried to free it, but as winter came it could not tilt toward the Sun to collect enough power. Its last message arrived on March 22, 2010, and NASA kept listening until 2011.
beats.now: It is still on Mars, exactly where it stopped.
beats.learned: Engineers rebuilt the sand trap on Earth to practice escape moves. That work shaped how later rovers are tested and driven.
